action: Section-by-section homepage audit, and the fixes
method: Fetched the rendered homepage from inside WordPress (the site is unreachable from the dev environment), then read the markup section by section: header, hero, rail, categories, method, featured guide, guides index, footer, head and JSON-LD.

findings.problem: No orderby in the query, so it fell back to date and showed the ten most recently imported Best Sellers under the heading 'What people actually buy'. The best-selling product on the site (24,889 orders) was not on the homepage.
findings.fix: Sorts on _lookdog_orders DESC with a date tiebreak. meta_key rather than meta_query so products with no recorded count sort last instead of dropping off.

findings.problem: Logo alt text was 'chatgpt image jul 5, 2026, 02 48 42 pm' - the raw AI filename, read aloud by screen readers and indexed as the logo's description.

A '7 new' badge in the Blog menu label, from an unmirrored mu-plugin. Matched on the literal title 'Blog', capped the count at 20, ran a post query on every nav render including footer menus, and carried inline orange styling.
findings.fix: scripts/lookdog-blog-badge.php corrects it at priority 20 - URL matching, uncapped count cached for an hour and busted on publish, site navigation only, class-based styling. The mu-plugin should be deleted by hand.

findings.problem: A Best Sellers card sat directly under the Best Sellers rail - the same 24 products, twice, adjacently, with near-identical copy ('What people actually buy' / 'The products people actually buy most').
findings.fix: Excluded from the grid. Six cards now.

findings.problem: Card blurbs were noun lists - 'Bowls, slow feeders and everyday care essentials' - which is what a shop writes. Every other line of copy on the site tells you how to choose.
findings.fix: Rewritten as one piece of real guidance each, drawn from the guide behind the category.

findings.problem: The section was raw inline-styled HTML in post_content, the only band not using the design system.
findings.fix: Now ld-band ld-band--tint with the standard wrap, plus a lede.

findings.problem: 'Explore by Category' is a heading any site could use.
findings.fix: 'Browse by what it is', paired with 'Or browse by what is going wrong' on the problems link - which names the site's two navigation axes.

findings.problem: The page stated its differentiator and never demonstrated it. Hero and method band both claim every listing names drawbacks; nothing on the page showed one.
findings.fix: New [lookdog_drawbacks] band, third on the page: four real Cons lines from four real product pages, credited and linked, one per category, rotating daily.

findings.problem: Tagline still read 'Smart dog accessories, product ideas and buying guides for happy dogs and their owners' - the positioning retired when the hero was rewritten.
findings.fix: Replaced with the current positioning plus the commission disclosure.

findings.problem: 'Quick Links' and 'Important Links' render as h2 and competed in the heading outline with real content headings.
The Shop menu listed six categories and nothing else - not Best Sellers, not the ten problem pages, not the guides.

WebSite, WebPage and Article all referenced https://lookdog.club#person for author, contributor and copyrightHolder, and no Person node existed in the graph. Three dangling @id references on every page.
findings.fix: All three point at the Organization, which is accurate - the byline is LookDog, there is no named person. The Person schema was removed. Verified: 4 nodes, 0 dangling references.

findings.problem: Organization.url was 'https://lookdog.club/ ' with a trailing space, shipped in the default schema.
findings.fix: Trimmed, and the trim runs across every field so it cannot come back.

findings.problem: description and slogan read 'Dog Accessory Guides & Product Picks' - an HTML entity stored in the site tagline option, encoded a second time on output.
Title and meta description still sold the retired positioning and did not match the H1.
findings.fix: 'LookDog | Dog Gear With the Drawbacks Written Down' (50 chars) and a matching description (148).

findings.problem: og:image was /2.jpg, an Astra starter photo shipped with the theme demo. That is what appeared when anyone shared the homepage.
findings.fix: The hero photograph, 1536x1024, with real alt text.

not_fixed.issue: No search anywhere on the site, with 167 products
not_fixed.note: The JSON-LD declares a SearchAction pointing at /?s=, so the endpoint exists and is advertised, but no visible search UI exists. Adding one means touching the Astra header builder, which is a bigger change than an audit fix and was left for a decision.
Workable but crowded. Grouping the six categories under one 'Shop' parent would halve it. Left alone because it changes how every visitor navigates.

not_fixed.issue: The featured guide band and the first row of the guides index are always the same post
not_fixed.note: The band shows the newest post and the index sorts newest-first, so the puppy guide appears twice in a row. Fixing it means the index skipping the featured post, which is a change to lookdog-home-guides.php and was noted rather than made.

not_fixed.issue: 20 inline style blocks and 20 stylesheets, 3 Google Fonts requests, no preloads
not_fixed.note: Mostly theme and plugin CSS. Our own shortcodes add gated blocks that only print where used.

list: ld-badge rendered twice (desktop and mobile nav, not footer)
rail leads with the 24,889-order cooling mat
verification.links: 37 unique internal links on the page, all 200
verification.design: check-design passes with no violations against lookdog-navy-ember
verification.caveat: No screenshot - lookdog.club is unreachable from the dev environment, whose egress policy answers 403 to CONNECT. Everything was verified by reading the rendered markup.
